The rules say "sits under Examples/ or SampleApp/" as a condition.

Wait — re-reading the rules: the restraint markers are the `is_*` context flags on participating records. The path-based check (`Examples/` or `SampleApp/`) is listed as a *description* of what `is_sample_app=true` typically means, not an independent trigger. The flags are authoritative. So `is_sample_app: false` means I should not apply the sample-app restraint for that record.

With no restraint markers triggered, I look at the actual cluster: these are empty-body extensions (and type aliases) across completely unrelated types (`IntentError`, `PlaybackError`, `PlaybackState`, `PlayerState`, `StreamingAudioState`, `TimeoutError`, `ProcessInfo.ThermalState`) in different packages (`Playback`, `DebugPanel`, `Wallpaper`, `Intents`). The `shared_field_count: 1` with empty `fields_or_signature` arrays and `differing_slots: null` suggests the structural similarity is purely coincidental — empty extensions that happen to share the same shape (nothing). These are domain-unrelated types whose structural coincidence is purely that they all have empty extensions.
